# What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet.

Day 2, 13:35 · Ryan Levering, Software Engineer · coverage: transcript, slides

Named in the previous speaker's hand-over ('Ryan is going to talk about how we are actually dealing with structured data'), heard clearly in a second attendee recording; he said he has been a software engineer at Google for about 15 years, focused on data ingestion.

## Claims

- **[Stage]** Search results have moved from ten blue links to feature-rich, media-rich results because users wanted more.
  <br><sub>`D2-C452` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · Extends [D1-C011](D1-S01-welcome-and-opening-keynotes.md) · Extends [D1-C158](D1-S01-welcome-and-opening-keynotes.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** AI Overviews and AI Mode launched as fairly text-heavy answers with little image content and few tables, and they have become more structured over time because that is what users want.
  <br><sub>`D2-C453` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs · Extends [D1-C011](D1-S01-welcome-and-opening-keynotes.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Structured data turns the loosely structured web into structured information that powers visual search features such as review stars and recipe filters (for example by preparation time).
  <br><sub>`D2-C454` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · confirmed by Google docs · [Introduction to structured data markup in Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data), [Review snippet (Review, AggregateRating) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/review-snippet) · Extended by [D3-C337](D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) · Used by the glossary term *Rich results*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Describing a page's content in a structured way lets Google understand and interpret that content more accurately.
  <br><sub>`D2-C455` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · confirmed by Google docs · [Introduction to structured data markup in Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data) · Used by the glossary term *Structured data*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Structured data can bring more qualified traffic, because the site can be shown in new, more interesting ways to more people, who are then more likely to click.
  <br><sub>`D2-C456` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · consistent with Google docs · [Introduction to structured data markup in Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Inside Google, views on structured data split into two camps: one says it is useless because models can generate it or read the page directly, the other says it is the future of machines talking to each other through MCP servers and new standards; the speaker said the truth is in the middle.
  <br><sub>`D2-C457` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer)</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google gave four reasons why structured data is still valuable even though models can extract information from pages: precision, extra content, efficiency and focus.
  <br><sub>`D2-C458` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Slide]** Structured data gives the high precision that complex schemas such as sale pricing need, with higher accuracy than large-scale extraction by large language models (LLMs).
  > "Structured data provides the high precision needed for complex schema (sale pricing), achieving higher accuracy than large-scale LLM extraction."
  <br><sub>`D2-C459` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** In the speaker's own tests, even the latest LLMs asked to generate schema.org markup for a page often invent properties that do not exist, get deeply nested schemas such as complex pricing models wrong, and duplicate content across several fields.
  <br><sub>`D2-C460` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs · Used by `DEV-SDA-11`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Automatic LLM extraction of structured information makes a great demo but is not yet good enough for extraction that aims at something like 99.9% accuracy, the speaker said.
  <br><sub>`D2-C461` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's guidance on generative AI content warns that AI output can contain hallucinations and says AI-generated metadata, including structured data and image alt text, should be fact-checked before publishing and the markup validated.
  <br><sub>`D2-C462` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. · is the documentation · [Google Search's guidance on using generative AI content on your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/using-gen-ai-content) · Extends [D1-C250](D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) · Extended by [D2-C947](D2-S14-lightning-session-f-media.md) · Extended by [D2-C952](D2-S14-lightning-session-f-media.md) · Extended by [D3-C686](D3-S18-wrapping-all-up-ai-search-and-making-sense-of-everything.md) · Used by `DEV-SDA-11`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Structured data often carries non-visible metadata that the page text lacks, such as full ISO dates or stable identifiers for user-generated content.
  > "It often contains non-visible metadata, such as full ISO dates or stable identifiers for UGC, that is not present in the page text."
  <br><sub>`D2-C463` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs · Used by `DEV-SDA-04`, `DEV-SDA-05`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's own extraction systems focus heavily on what is visible on a page, which improves precision but means they can miss content or interpret it incorrectly.
  <br><sub>`D2-C464` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Gemini in Chrome relies heavily on the screenshot it takes of a page.
  <br><sub>`D2-C465` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · consistent with Google docs · [Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) · Extends [D1-C131](D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Used by `DEV-HTM-04`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Markup can state a date as a full ISO 8601 value, which disambiguates a visible date whose local time zone Google might not detect correctly; this matters for event extraction and wherever the date must be exactly right.
  <br><sub>`D2-C466` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · consistent with Google docs · [Event (Event) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/event) · Used by `DEV-SDA-05`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's structured data documentation says not to mark up content that is not visible to readers of the page, and not to add structured data about information that users cannot see even if it is accurate.
  > "don't add structured data about information that is not visible to the user, even if the information is accurate"
  <br><sub>`D2-C467` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. · is the documentation · [Introduction to structured data markup in Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data), [General structured data guidelines](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/sd-policies) · Used by `DEV-SDA-02`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** The 'non-visible metadata' argument is not a licence to mark up hidden content, since Google's structured data guidelines still require markup to describe what users can see; use markup for the machine-precise form of facts the page shows, such as a full ISO date with time zone for a visible event date or a homepage url for a named organisation.
  <br><sub>`D2-C468` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. · [General structured data guidelines](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/sd-policies), [Introduction to structured data markup in Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data) · Used by `DEV-SDA-02`, `DEV-SDA-04`, `DEV-SDA-05`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Parsing structured data is significantly cheaper and more efficient than relying on LLMs for every complex extraction task.
  <br><sub>`D2-C469` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs · Repeated by [D3-C405](D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Even Google cannot afford to run complex AI models on every page in its index, and distilling them into cheaper models makes them less precise.
  <br><sub>`D2-C470` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Rule-based parsing of markup is nearly free by comparison with AI models, so Google will always prefer extracting information from structured data over model-based extraction.
  > "So we're always going to prefer that particular approach."
  <br><sub>`D2-C471` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Do not drop markup on the assumption that AI reads the page anyway: by Google's own account LLM extraction is not precise enough for prices and nested offers and too costly to run on every page, so explicit markup remains the dependable route for those facts.
  <br><sub>`D2-C472` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet.</sub>

- **[Slide]** Structured data explicitly points to the pertinent data on a page, which reduces noise and stops Google's systems from pulling in extraneous information such as prices of related products.
  <br><sub>`D2-C473` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs · Used by `DEV-SDA-07`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's systems sometimes fail to determine a page's main content correctly, and structured data helps because site owners tend to mark up what is actually important rather than boilerplate or ads.
  <br><sub>`D2-C474` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs · Extends [D2-C028](D2-S03-how-is-html-interpreted.md) · Used by `DEV-SDA-07`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** On product pages with related-product or recently-viewed carousels, make sure the Product markup describes only the main item and its price; Google's own example of what markup prevents was pulling a price from related products.
  <br><sub>`D2-C475` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. · Used by `DEV-SDA-07`</sub>

- **[Stage]** The structured data Google processes is not fed very differently to AI Overviews and AI Mode: after cleaning and quality work, the same data goes to both the classic results page and the AI features.
  <br><sub>`D2-C476` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · consistent with Google docs · [AI features and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), [Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) · Extends [D1-C038](D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) · Used by `DEV-AIF-02`</sub>

- **[Stage]** As far as the speaker knows, in most of Google's main AI uses a page's schema.org markup is not turned into text and put directly into the model's context; the data is first sorted out, checked for quality and indexed before it is passed on as grounding context.
  <br><sub>`D2-C477` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs · Extends [D1-C061](D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** The speaker said there are concerns that feeding raw schema.org markup straight into an AI model's context would be a big abuse vector, one reason Google does not do so.
  <br><sub>`D2-C478` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Analysis]** There is no separate markup for AI features: by Google's account the same processed markup feeds classic results and AI answers, and raw schema.org is generally not passed into model context, so invest in the types Google documents for its features rather than in extra markup written for AI.
  <br><sub>`D2-C479` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. · Used by `DEV-AIF-02`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's guide to optimizing for generative AI features lists 'overfocusing on structured data' among the things site owners don't need to do: structured data is not required for generative AI search and no special schema.org markup is needed, though it remains worth using because it helps pages become eligible for rich results.

- **[Stage]** Google will never penalise a site just for having more structured data on its pages than Google uses; extra markup does not hurt.
  > "we will never penalize you for having more structured data on your pages"
  <br><sub>`D2-C488` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · consistent with Google docs · [Introduction to structured data markup in Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data) · Used by `DEV-SDA-03`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's structured data types fall roughly into two groups: broad page-level types such as breadcrumbs and article, and vertical-specific types such as recipes, events and products.
  <br><sub>`D2-C491` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · consistent with Google docs · [Structured data markup that Google Search supports](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/search-gallery)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Pick only the structured data types that are relevant to a page instead of adding every type Google is interested in.
  <br><sub>`D2-C492` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · consistent with Google docs · [General structured data guidelines](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/sd-policies) · Used by `DEV-SDA-03`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Most sites now run on content management systems whose plug-ins generate the markup, so check that the plug-ins in your stack produce good markup, for example a calendar plug-in that outputs event markup.
  <br><sub>`D2-C493` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · consistent with Google docs · [Introduction to structured data markup in Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google accepts three structured data syntaxes, JSON-LD, microdata and RDFa, which are all valid and are extracted at the very start into the same pipelines, so they are interpreted identically downstream.
  <br><sub>`D2-C494` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · consistent with Google docs · [Introduction to structured data markup in Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data), [General structured data guidelines](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/sd-policies) · Used by `DEV-SDA-01`, the glossary term *JSON-LD*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google recommends JSON-LD because it is one contiguous block that is easier to author, so people make fewer mistakes with it.
  <br><sub>`D2-C495` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · confirmed by Google docs · [Introduction to structured data markup in Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data) · Used by `DEV-SDA-01`, the glossary term *JSON-LD*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Microdata has an advantage when payload size matters: embedded in the existing HTML, it avoids duplicating the page content in a separate JSON-LD block.
  <br><sub>`D2-C496` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs · Used by `DEV-SDA-01`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Default to JSON-LD and switch to microdata only where page weight is critical, since Google interprets all three syntaxes identically and JSON-LD is the one people get wrong least often.
  <br><sub>`D2-C497` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. · Used by `DEV-SDA-01`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google recommends testing and previewing structured data in the Rich Results Test, which shows the rich result features it detected and whether the markup is valid.
  <br><sub>`D2-C498` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · confirmed by Google docs · [Rich Results Test](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7445569?hl=en), [Introduction to structured data markup in Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data) · Used by `DEV-SDA-11`, the glossary term *Rich Results Test*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Test structured data manually first and only then put it into the site's templates.
  <br><sub>`D2-C499` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · consistent with Google docs · [Introduction to structured data markup in Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data) · Used by `DEV-SDA-11`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Structured data that is not relevant to the page's content can be treated as abusive: Google's filters make it ineffective, and egregious cases can lead to a manual action.
  <br><sub>`D2-C500` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · confirmed by Google docs · [General structured data guidelines](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/sd-policies) · Extended by [D3-C647](D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) · Used by `DEV-SDA-02`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's general structured data guidelines say a structured data manual action removes a page's eligibility for rich results but does not affect how the page ranks in web search.
  <br><sub>`D2-C501` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. · is the documentation · [General structured data guidelines](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/sd-policies) · Used by `DEV-SDA-02`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Use unique identifiers in structured data, for example the homepage URL in an organisation's url property, so Google can tell which specific entity is meant rather than reading just a name string.
  <br><sub>`D2-C502` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · confirmed by Google docs · [Organization (Organization) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/organization) · Used by `DEV-SDA-04`, `DEV-SDA-09`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Several plug-ins emitting the same markup type is one of the most common structured data problems: the duplicates can make an event details page look like a list of events and change how Google interprets the page.
  <br><sub>`D2-C503` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs · Used by `DEV-SDA-06`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Audit CMS templates for duplicate markup by running one page per template through the Rich Results Test and checking whether an SEO plug-in and a theme or events plug-in emit the same type twice; 'more markup never hurts' covers relevant, non-duplicated markup only.
  <br><sub>`D2-C504` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. · Used by `DEV-SDA-06`</sub>

(Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · consistent with Google docs · [Merchant listing (Product, Offer) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/merchant-listing), [Latest documentation updates](https://developers.google.com/search/updates) · Extended by [D3-C396](D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) · Used by `DEV-SDA-08`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's documentation updates log calls the July 2026 sale price change a clarification: a new Sale duration section of the merchant listing guide explains validFrom with validThrough or priceValidUntil, aligned with Merchant Center's sale_price_effective_date attribute.
  <br><sub>`D2-C507` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. · is the documentation · [Latest documentation updates](https://developers.google.com/search/updates), [Merchant listing (Product, Offer) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/merchant-listing) · Used by `DEV-SDA-08`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** For time-limited sales, give the sale price its validity dates in the product markup (Google's merchant listing documentation describes validFrom, validThrough and priceValidUntil) instead of editing markup by hand when the sale ends, and keep the dates aligned with the Merchant Center feed.
  <br><sub>`D2-C508` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. · [Merchant listing (Product, Offer) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/merchant-listing), [Latest documentation updates](https://developers.google.com/search/updates) · Used by `DEV-SDA-08`</sub>

- **[Stage]** More shopping structured data news was left for a Day 3 talk by a Google colleague, Alex.
  <br><sub>`D2-C509` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · Extended by [D3-C365](D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Schema.org, in which Google is a major participant, began publishing usage statistics for all its types and properties in 2026, showing in buckets how many domains use each one; the data is also in schema.org's GitHub repository.
  <br><sub>`D2-C510` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google often needs to see a markup type adopted on websites before it invests in a feature that uses it, a chicken-and-egg problem that the schema.org usage statistics are meant to help break.
  <br><sub>`D2-C511` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs · Extends [D1-C120](D1-S12-q-a.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Schema.org added support for RDF lists and sets, which give a way to express ordered values, because RDF triples are not ordered by nature.
  <br><sub>`D2-C512` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Markup for schema.org types that Google does not use yet is a bet on future features; check a type's usage bucket on schema.org before investing, since adoption is what Google says it watches before building a feature.
  <br><sub>`D2-C513` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet.</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google announced server-side structured data validation as coming soon: it will publish downloadable validation rules in SHACL on each structured data feature guide, with other kinds of checks to follow.
  <br><sub>`D2-C514` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs · Used by `DEV-SDA-12`, the glossary term *SHACL*</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's planned validation workflow has five steps: download the rules from the feature guide, generate the JSON or embedded microdata or RDFa, run the rules against the generated server-side markup as a first check, deploy and test in the Rich Results Test, and monitor ongoing performance in Search Console.
  <br><sub>`D2-C515` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs · Used by `DEV-SDA-12`</sub>

- **[Stage]** The SHACL rules are meant to run inside a site's content generation, so markup is sanity-checked before it is published and does not silently regress later, a breakage site owners might otherwise discover only through a Search Console report.
  <br><sub>`D2-C516` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs · Used by `DEV-SDA-12`, the glossary term *SHACL*</sub>

- **[Stage]** The SHACL rules will not replace Search Console as the canonical place for structured data reports, because some checks use Google's internal libraries and cannot be expressed in SHACL, but they will catch problems such as a missing required field.
  <br><sub>`D2-C517` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs · Used by `DEV-SDA-12`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's example SHACL shape for Event requires a name, treats a missing description only as a warning, and accepts the image either as an ImageObject or as a URL.
  <br><sub>`D2-C518` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · consistent with Google docs · [Event (Event) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/event)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google plans a SHACL rule set for each of its structured data feature types and will release the rule sets gradually once they have been checked.
  <br><sub>`D2-C519` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · not in Google docs · Used by `DEV-SDA-12`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** When the SHACL rules appear, wire them into the build or CMS publishing step as an automated test, so a template change that drops a required property fails before deployment instead of surfacing weeks later in Search Console.
  <br><sub>`D2-C520` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. · Used by `DEV-SDA-12`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Structured data makes pages eligible to appear as rich results, Google's structured data talk said in its recap.
  <br><sub>`D2-C521` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · consistent with Google docs · [Introduction to structured data markup in Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/intro-structured-data), [General structured data guidelines](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/sd-policies) · Extends [D1-C122](D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Extended by [D3-C324](D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) · Used by the glossary term *Rich results*, the glossary term *Structured data*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google keeps adding structured data features and recommendations but also removes them: in the previous year (2025) it removed several features that brought little benefit and were little used.
  <br><sub>`D2-C522` · Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. (Ryan Levering, Software Engineer) · confirmed by Google docs · [Simplifying the search results page](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2025/06/simplifying-search-results) · Used by `DEV-SDA-03`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's merchant listing guide says Product rich results only support pages that focus on a single product, or on several variants of the same product.
  <br><sub>`D2-C834` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. · is the documentation · [Merchant listing (Product, Offer) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/merchant-listing) · Used by `DEV-SDA-07`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's merchant listing guide warns that a listing may not display if its priceValidUntil property indicates a past date.
  <br><sub>`D2-C835` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. · is the documentation · [Merchant listing (Product, Offer) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/merchant-listing) · Used by `DEV-SDA-08`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's Event structured data guide says to give a date without a time, such as 2019-08-15, when the start hour is not known, and to include the UTC or GMT offset whenever a time is given.
  <br><sub>`D2-C836` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet. · is the documentation · [Event (Event) structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/event) · Used by `DEV-SDA-05`</sub>
